headline: Indonesia Ministry Of Marine Affairs Advances Ocean Policy Reform
seoTitle: Indonesia Ministry Of Marine Affairs Ocean Policy
metaDescription: Indonesia's Ministry of Marine Affairs issued 834 maritime space usage permits and new blue carbon regulations to boost investment and conservation.
aiSummaryBullets: The ministry issued 834 permits for maritime space utilization to increase investment and non-tax state revenue.
New regulations under Minister Regulation Number 17 of 2026 aim to manage blue carbon economic value for ecosystem protection.
The government maintains its long-term goal of designating 97.5 million hectares as marine conservation areas by 2045.
aiContextParagraph: The Indonesian Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries has introduced several regulatory measures in 2026 aimed at balancing economic growth with environmental sustainability. Officials recently announced the issuance of 834 maritime space utilization permits to drive domestic investment and increase non-tax state revenue. Simultaneously, the ministry has formalized the management of blue carbon economic value through the implementation of Minister Regulation Number 17 of 2026, which focuses on protecting marine ecosystems. These efforts complement the government's broader strategy to expand its marine conservation footprint, with a stated target of reaching 97.5 million hectares of protected waters by 2045. Current progress includes the establishment of 31 million hectares of conservation zones. Additionally, the ministry is implementing programs designed to improve the welfare of approximately 3.2 million fishermen across the country as part of its ongoing sectoral development strategy.
whyItIsViral: The topic is experiencing moderate attention, covered by four independent news outlets, indicating ongoing institutional focus on maritime management.
